text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,255.05, up 0.84% for the day and 0.9% over the past five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 0.9% (advances 355 vs declines 134). Breadth was “healthy” with a score of 73 and 80.6% of stocks above their 20‑day moving average, showing the rally was fairly wide‑spread. Bank Nifty outperformed, gaining 1.76% to 60,792.4, and the India VIX, a volatility gauge, ticked higher to 17.56 (+0.77%).  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding INR 12,563.33 crore today, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 8,434.53 crore, extending a ten‑day FII buying streak. Leading sectors were PSU banks, capital markets, private banks, auto and consumption, whereas media, pharma and IT showed weakness. In the options market, Nifty’s put‑call ratio (PCR) is 0.77, indicating more call than put interest; the “max pain” level sits at 25,100, with a call wall at 26,000 and a put wall at 24,500. Bank Nifty’s PCR is 1.17, suggesting slightly more put pressure, with max pain at 58,000 and a call wall at 60,500.  

Watch the 25,258 pivot (P) and the first support at 25,092 on Nifty; a break below could test the 24,500 put wall. For Bank Nifty, the pivot at 60,854 and support at 60,314 are key, while the 61,400 level is a fresh target mentioned in market commentary. Keep an eye on FII flows, crude oil easing (Brent $94.1) and the rupee near 93.68, as they can influence sentiment in the next session.
